title: Government may allow fees on UPI payment above Rs 2,000
description: The government may allow a small charge on UPI payments exceeding two thousand rupees. This levy would apply to transactions made to businesses and not individuals. Industry experts anticipate a possible ceiling on the absolute amount charged for these transactions.

title: 2 ISI-backed terror modules busted: Pistols, petrol bombs seized, 9 arrested
description: Punjab Police apprehended nine individuals, including four juveniles, in two ISI-backed terror modules.  Authorities recovered illegal firearms, petrol bombs, and a stolen motorcycle from the arrested suspects.  The accused were reportedly recruiting local youth for terror activities and conducting surveillance.  These individuals acted at the behest of handlers from the Inter-Services Intelligence agency.  The police operation successfully dismantled these cross-border terror networks.

title: Heavens won’t fall if all 6 Vande stanzas sung in madrassas: Calcutta HC
description: The Calcutta High Court heard a public interest litigation challenging mandatory Vande Mataram stanzas.  The court questioned the necessity of forcing students to sing specific religious or nationalistic songs.  Arguments were made that forcing the song could disrupt communal harmony and lead to legal issues.  The court noted that no coercive steps have been taken regarding the notification yet.  Additional Solicitor General opposed the interim prayer, calling some PILs publicity-driven.

title: 22-year-old suspect in teenager's rape lynched by mob in Jharkhand; 8 arrested
description: A 22-year-old man accused of abduction and sexual assault died after being beaten. Villagers attacked him with fists, kicks, and sticks following the girl's allegations. Police rescued the man and took him to a local hospital for treatment. Eight individuals were arrested late Tuesday in connection with the lynching incident. Additional forces have been deployed amid tension, and the situation is under control.

description: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution, will close in June after a decade of operation. This school provided education, healthcare, and family support to low-income children. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative will not continue funding beyond the upcoming academic year. Academic results remained below state averages, prompting the board's decision. The initiative pledged fifty million dollars to aid the transition for affected students.

title: US govt may soon increase H-1B and L-1 visas fees for large companies
description: The US government plans to expand an additional fee for certain visa petitions. This fee currently applies to initial H-1B and L-1 visa grants. The proposed change will extend this charge to petitions for extensions of stay. Companies with over fifty employees and a majority on these visas will be affected. This expansion aims to fund biometric entry-exit systems and other government programs.

title: As France sees its first fire cloud, should India be worried?
description: France witnessed its first pyrocumulonimbus fire cloud event in July 2026.  This phenomenon occurs when intense wildfires create their own thunderstorms.  India's rising temperatures and dry spells increase forest fire frequency.  While India has not reported fire clouds, its forests are becoming more flammable.  The Himalayan pine belt presents the highest potential for such an event in India.

title: 'Not our draft': Netanyahu rejects Trump's Gaza plan
description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has openly recognized the existing rifts with U.S. President Donald Trump. He emphasized that for any reconstruction efforts in Gaza to commence, Hamas needs to be completely disarmed. Furthermore, the Board of Peace has declared that Israeli forces will maintain their position and not retreat beyond the Yellow Line until all weaponry in Gaza is dismantled.

Protesters alleged police lathicharged them and used water cannons on women. The Karni Sena demanded withdrawal of UGC guidelines and other changes. They vowed to continue protests on streets for justice.
